rationale: fastdiff_flow_pixel_constrained-claude-agentic: image_size=512, pixel_spacing=0.3516, n_angles=128, n_det=1024, det_spacing=0.35754, sod=500.0, sdd=1000.0, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.5, train_n=400, val_n=200, noise_i0=100000.0, noise_sigma_e=10.0, seed=42, dataset_kind=breast_ct, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_pixel_breast.pt, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.05, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=30, fd_recon_dc_relax=1.0, rationale=iter-5 EXPLORATORY DC-strength combo (dc_n_cg 5->30 + dc_relax 0.5->1.0) on the near-FBP init_t0.05 base. SIX-BOX: (1)PRIOR: init_t axis fully mapped and MONOTONIC to the FBP floor: 0.7->0.05 gave rmse 0.0428->0.0264->0.0144->0.00669 (ssim 0.427->0.915), converging TO the 128-view breast FBP (rmse0.00521, ssim0.920) from ABOVE. hr=0 throughout: the breast-native prior cannot EXCEED the near-oracle sparse-view FBP. (2)FAILURE / OPEN QUESTION: at init_t0.05 the prior barely acts, so recon ~ DC-projected FBP. The ONLY way to beat the FBP is if a DEEP data-consistency CG solve finds a lower-rmse data-consistent image than the analytic FBP. In the Mayo sibling dc_n_cg was the ONLY lever that moved rmse. (3)ONE KNOB (DC-strength, combined): dc_n_cg 5->30 AND dc_relax 0.5->1.0 (full deep CG projection). (4)HYPOTHESIS: if full deep DC at near-FBP init STILL cannot push rmse below 0.00521, the regime-bound ceiling is PROVEN at the DC limit: the data-consistent solution the constrained flow converges to IS the FBP; a prior has no sparse-view-noise headroom to exploit at 128 views. (5)BUDGET: 30 CG x 8 steps x 200 slices, CG cheap fwd/back-proj, inside 20-min. (6)Serial.
